text:
Boone Jenner spent 808 games and a long run as captain in Columbus before landing in Washington this season, and at 33 he's doing what he's always done: scoring a few, killing penalties, and showing up on the forecheck. Six goals in 19 games puts him on a decent pace, though the assists (two) are thin.

His finishing is running slightly ahead of his chances (six goals on 4.25 expected), while the Capitals have scored about four fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, so the two roughly cancel out. At five-on-five Washington breaks even on expected goals with him out there, a little worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey saw more last season, rating him a play driver in the 89th percentile among forwards after adjusting for his teammates in Columbus.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has always caught his style: 62% of his shots came off the rush, and he dumps the puck in rather than carrying it. He ranks 102nd in the league in wins added by goals. A steady veteran on a new team, finding his place.
headline: Jenner's first season outside Columbus
